assessments.reasoning: Both original acquisitions returned complete bodies with HTTP 200. The reported SHA-256 of the 1,846-byte revision-2 claim matches claim_sha256. The 11,358-byte English license from the ASF's apache/www-site repository at commit 01b1be9fbc5cd93b6794f5653a58b9b863807f84 identifies itself as version 2.0, January 2004. Its reported SHA-256, cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30, matches the claim's provenance. The reported §4(d) byte range [5748, 6853) spans 1,105 bytes and its SHA-256, aca09ce84f2a9ebbb942e5879d214951fc13c88a4df68667cf2efab482db05a4, matches the specified digest. The paragraph directly supports the revision-2 claim's trigger, attribution scope, and placement alternatives.

challenge.method: Compared the reopened claim with the complete §4(d) paragraph, the §1 definition, and adjacent §4(c). Tested the display option by changing who generates the display, the documentation option by supplying a manual with the derivative, and the trigger by removing the upstream NOTICE.
challenge.results: A readable copy on the derivative's own customary third-party credits display qualifies. An unrelated website that generates its own credits page fails the display condition even if the page reproduces every relevant attribution. A manual supplied with the derivative qualifies independently. Without an upstream NOTICE, §4(d) imposes no duty to create one. Section 4(c) can still require retention, in distributed derivative Source, of pertinent copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from the upstream Source. The informational status of NOTICE contents leaves the copying condition intact. No contrary evidence appeared for the claim within its stated scope.

limitations: This finding covers the stated assertion in the January 2004 English plaintext edition of Apache License 2.0.

Section 1 covers works in Source or Object form based on the licensed Work whose modifications, taken together, constitute original authorship. It excludes works that remain separable and works whose only connection is linking or binding by name to interfaces of the Work or its derivatives.

Applying the condition to a particular distribution would require facts about the works, the upstream NOTICE, the relevance of its entries, and how the copy is supplied. Other redistribution conditions and ASF release policies have separate scopes.
reasoning: Revision 2 of apache-20-section-4d-notice-attributions preserves the conditions in §4(d). When the upstream Work is distributed with a NOTICE text file and a licensee distributes Derivative Works, the licensee must include a readable copy of every attribution in that file that pertains to any part of the distributed derivative. At least one permitted location suffices. The copy may appear in a NOTICE text file included in the derivative distribution, in Source or documentation supplied with the derivative, or in a display the derivative itself generates, if and wherever third-party notices of that kind ordinarily appear.
